official.description_text:
Postdoc in cyber-physical security for smart grids
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
As power systems become more digitalised and rely increasingly on synchronised measurements, protecting monitoring data and communications is essential for reliable grid operation. The research will focus on threats such as time-synchronisation attacks and manipulation of monitoring data in wide-area monitoring systems, characterization of their impact on system operation, and their timely detection using machine learning algorithms. The postdoc will develop methods for detection and resilience, and collaborate with an international team to validate them in cyber-physical power-system scenarios.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made
Strong publication track record in leading conferences and/or journals in a relevant research field
As the work involves international cooperation, excellent skills in English are required, both oral and in writing
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience with simulation-based on experimental validation
The ability to work in a team as well as independently
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Name and email address of two references.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.
A

is a time-limited qualified appointment focusing mainly on research, intended as a first career step after a dissertation.

ai.summary: A postdoctoral position at KTH's School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science focused on cyber-physical security for smart grids, involving detection and resilience methods for time-synchronisation attacks and monitoring data manipulation in wide-area systems, validated through simulation and machine learning.

thematic_fit.rationale: The position is fundamentally about cyber-physical security, power systems, and attack detection via machine learning. While 'machine learning' may appear tangentially relevant, the core research direction (critical infrastructure security, grid resilience, adversarial system dynamics) has no thematic overlap with human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, collaboration, wayfinding, or any of the researcher's stated domains. No HCI, user evaluation, or immersive systems component.

methodological_fit.rationale: The posting emphasizes 'simulation-based and experimental validation' and 'machine learning algorithms', both of which the researcher has encountered but not in substantial depth. The researcher has beginner-level Python and no stated background in cybersecurity, power systems, or machine learning development. The methodological core (security analysis, adversarial testing, control-system dynamics) is orthogonal to the researcher's experimental and HCI evaluation expertise.

growth_value.rationale: This role would develop skills in cyber-physical security, machine learning, and power-systems simulation—none of which align with the researcher's stated capability gaps or target identity. The excluded_directions in the profile do not explicitly rule out ML, but the researcher's trajectory is human-centred systems research, not algorithmic development. This represents a significant pivot away from core research interests.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a leading technical university in Sweden (a preferred country in the profile). It is not listed as Priority 1 (Aalto, TU Delft) or Priority 2 (Tampere, other ≥70% fit groups), but Sweden is geographically and linguistically aligned. The SEOCS (School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science) is internationally recognized. However, strategic value is substantially diminished by the research direction mismatch—proximity to target geography does not offset absence of methodological and thematic alignment.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD or equivalent; researcher currently holds MSc by Research (in progress). Eligibility contingent on completion and conferral before employment start.

Position calls for 'strong publication track record in leading conferences/journals in a relevant research field.' Researcher has 1 first-author journal article and 1 systematic mapping review (in progress)—possibly below the bar for 'strong' record at postdoc level.
Preferred qualification: PhD obtained within last 3 years. Researcher must complete MSc first; timeline unclear.
No stated background in cybersecurity, power systems, control systems, or applied machine learning; significant onboarding risk.
risks: Fundamental mismatch in research domain. Position is cyber-physical security for critical infrastructure; researcher's expertise and identity are human-centred immersive systems.
Skill gap in Python and machine learning at the depth required for the role; researcher is beginner in Python and has no stated ML algorithm development experience.

Not a methodological fit despite mentioning simulation and machine learning. The underlying research culture (security, control systems, adversarial testing) differs substantially from HCI and immersive systems evaluation.
Taking this role would sideline the researcher's doctoral pathway in human-centred XR for 2 years, delaying re-entry to the target domain.
Publication track record may be assessed as junior relative to typical postdoc candidates in cybersecurity.
